To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the risk factor assessment in women with coronary artery disease is different from the risk factor assessment of men.

(a) chest pain is a major problem in women, (b) the presentation of coronary disease in women may differ from that of males, (c) the risk factor profile in women differs, (d) metabolic syndrome is a major risk factor for coronary artery disease in women, and (e) microvascular dysfunction may be an important mechanism of ischemia.
women with coronary artery disease have a different presentation, different risk factors and different mechanisms of disease, compared to their male counterparts.
